The '''Treaty Accord of 1951''' was the postwar diplomatic process that produced the Istragarde settlement after the [[Avant Great War]] and [[Continuation War]]. It is treated here as the settlement conference and accord process, while the [[Treaty of the Concord of Istragarde]] refers to the legal framework and treaty text that came from it.

== Background ==

By 1951, the victorious powers and newly independent states faced exhaustion, destroyed infrastructure, population displacement, and competing territorial claims. The defeat of the [[Vesperan Empire]] had removed the old imperial order without creating a strong replacement.

== Settlement Goals ==

The accord attempted to recognize postwar borders, establish arbitration, discourage renewed aggression, manage maritime claims, and create procedures for humanitarian and weapons disputes.

The resulting system was intentionally limited. States wanted stability, but few were willing to surrender sovereignty to a powerful world government after years of total war.

== Weaknesses ==

The accord's weakness became one of its defining traits. The Istragarde framework relied heavily on voluntary compliance, which allowed later states to ignore rulings, exploit territorial clauses, or use legal language to justify aggression.

== Legacy ==

The Treaty Accord of 1951 prevented immediate postwar collapse but left enough ambiguity for later disputes, including Khalindarian claims, [[People's Republic of Mariposa|Mariposian]] maritime tensions, and expansionist doctrines in the 1970s-1990s.
